whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the MuleSoft Platform Architect exam?

personas.label: Platform architects
personas.description: You decide where Mule applications run and how Anypoint Platform is structured and governed across teams.

personas.label: Infrastructure engineers
personas.description: You design networking, runtime isolation, availability, and operational support for integration platforms.

personas.label: IT directors and technical leads
personas.description: You set platform standards, help teams work within them, and own platform planning and budgets.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the MuleSoft Platform Architect exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam focuses on platform design more than writing integrations. You need to choose deployment, networking, availability, and governance designs that meet organizational constraints.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
70% to pass, which is 42 correct answers out of 60.
Infrastructure topics: Review VPCs, load balancing, clustering, and failover.
Several disciplines: Networking, security, operations, and governance all affect the architecture.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice selecting a deployment model from constraints and explaining how traffic reaches the application. Also explain what happens to data and scheduled work when a node or region fails. Aim for at least 80% on practice questions.

examFormat.heading: MuleSoft Platform Architect exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Questions describe platform constraints and ask which architecture meets them.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios may require on-premises data residency, fixed IP addresses, high availability, or delegated access across business units.
bestWayToPass: Compare deployment options: Review CloudHub, Runtime Fabric, and customer-hosted runtimes and how they place control and runtime responsibilities.
Trace the network path: Understand VPCs, VPN or peering, load balancers, custom domains, and TLS termination.
Plan for availability: Consider replicas, clustering, persistent queues, and what survives a node failure.
Apply governance: Learn how business groups, environments, roles, and API policies support separate teams and consistent standards.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Anypoint Platform architecture, including deployment models, network design, availability, API governance, and team administration. The guide allows up to five non-scored questions. The exam is 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, with a 70% pass mark, weighted towards Governing web APIs on Anypoint Platform (17%) and Designing APIs using System, Process, and Experience Layers (12%).

blocks.heading: Control Plane and Runtime Plane
blocks.body: The control plane provides tools to design, manage, and monitor APIs and applications. The runtime plane is where Mule applications execute. In managed cloud deployments, MuleSoft operates both planes. With Runtime Fabric, the control plane can remain in Anypoint while the runtime plane runs in customer-managed infrastructure. A customer-hosted runtime gives the customer more operational responsibility. For data residency and control questions, identify where each plane and the application data will reside.

blocks.heading: Choosing a Deployment Model
blocks.body: CloudHub provides a managed runtime option. Runtime Fabric supports deployments to customer-managed infrastructure such as Kubernetes while retaining Anypoint Platform management. Customer-hosted runtimes suit organizations that need to manage the runtime environment themselves. Choose based on network access, data residency, operational skills, availability, and the required management model.

blocks.heading: Networking and Ingress
blocks.body: Anypoint VPC provides an isolated network for CloudHub applications and can connect to private infrastructure through supported VPN or peering arrangements. A load balancer can provide ingress and, depending on the option, fixed IP addresses, custom domains, and TLS configuration. Trace how requests enter the network and how the application reaches back-end systems. Avoid exposing private databases directly to the public internet.

blocks.heading: Availability and Disaster Recovery
blocks.body: Availability design may use replicas, clustering, redundant infrastructure, and persistent messaging. Persistent queues or Anypoint MQ can protect messages when a consumer restarts. Clustered runtimes can coordinate work such as scheduled tasks so it runs once where configured. Disaster recovery starts by setting recovery time and recovery point objectives: acceptable downtime and data loss. A second region or traffic switching plan may be needed in addition to backups.

blocks.heading: Governance, Security, and Monitoring
blocks.body: Business groups organize platform assets and access for teams. Environments separate lifecycle stages such as development and production. Roles and permissions control who can administer or deploy to each area. API Manager policies can enforce client identity consistently, while API Governance checks specifications against standards. Anypoint Visualizer helps show application and API dependencies, and Anypoint Monitoring supports operational dashboards and alerts.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the MuleSoft Platform Architect exam
scenarioTips.intro: Start with the non-negotiable constraints: data location, network access, uptime, recovery, team separation, and deployment approvals. Choose the simplest platform design that meets them.

blocks.heading: Select a Deployment Model
blocks.body: Use managed cloud when it meets requirements; consider Runtime Fabric when workloads must run on customer-managed infrastructure; use customer-hosted runtimes when the customer operates the runtime.

blocks.heading: Design High Availability
blocks.body: Consider replicas or clusters, persistent messaging, and how scheduled work is coordinated. A backup alone does not provide a complete recovery design.

blocks.heading: Set Disaster Recovery Targets
blocks.body: Define acceptable downtime and data loss, then design failover and recovery procedures to meet those targets.

blocks.heading: Apply Platform Governance
blocks.body: Use business groups and environments for organizational separation, roles for access control, and API Governance for consistent specification standards.

blocks.heading: Monitor and Scale
blocks.body: Use monitoring alerts to detect error-rate or performance changes. For stateless workloads, scaling out with additional replicas may be a simple first step.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials for MuleSoft platform architects
nextCertsAfter.intro: Continue with a MuleSoft integration architecture or platform operations credential.

sampleQuestions.question: A regulated integration must keep its data plane inside the customer network while Anypoint Platform manages its lifecycle. Which deployment model fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Runtime Fabric keeps the runtime on customer-managed infrastructure and connects it to Anypoint Platform for management.
whyWrong: A load balancer handles traffic but does not host the runtime.
Design Center is for API design rather than customer-managed execution.
Runtime Fabric runs applications on customer infrastructure with Anypoint management.

sampleQuestions.question: A partner requires a fixed source IP and a custom API domain with the company’s certificate. What platform component should the architect consider?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A dedicated load balancer can support custom domains, certificates, and fixed IP requirements.
whyWrong: vCore size changes compute, not the required network ingress features.
A dedicated load balancer can support fixed IPs, custom domains, and certificates.
An additional replica improves capacity or availability but not ingress identity.

sampleQuestions.question: CloudHub applications must access a database on the company’s private network. What should be configured?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Anypoint VPC with a supported VPN or peering connection provides private network access to the database.
whyWrong: A public endpoint would expose the database rather than provide private connectivity.
A VPC with VPN or peering can connect CloudHub to the private network.
A worker size does not create a network route to the database.

sampleQuestions.question: A two-node Mule deployment must remain available during a node outage and run its scheduled job only once. What design addresses both needs?
options: Run the scheduler on every node
sampleQuestions.explanation: A cluster can provide node resilience, and coordinated primary-node scheduling prevents every node from running the same scheduled task.
whyWrong: Running the scheduler on all nodes may duplicate the job.
A cluster can coordinate redundancy and primary-node scheduling.
A single server remains a point of failure.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement distinguishes the control plane from the runtime plane?
options: Both always run in MuleSoft’s cloud
The runtime plane is where APIs are designed
They are two names for the same component
sampleQuestions.explanation: The control plane manages platform assets and operations; the runtime plane executes Mule applications.
whyWrong: The control and runtime planes can be separated and placed according to the deployment model.
The runtime plane executes applications; it does not design APIs.
The control and runtime planes have different responsibilities.

sampleQuestions.question: Five business units need separate environments and access control under one company platform agreement. What should be used?
options: A separate Anypoint account for each unit
sampleQuestions.explanation: Business groups organize platform assets and access for different teams or units.
whyWrong: Business groups can separate teams under one platform agreement.
One shared environment does not provide the requested team separation.
Load balancers route network traffic rather than organize platform permissions.

sampleQuestions.question: Orders must remain available for processing if the receiving application restarts. What should the design include?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Persistent queues or Anypoint MQ can retain messages across application restarts for later processing.
whyWrong: Replicas alone do not preserve in-flight messages across restarts.
Heap size does not persist messages when an application restarts.
In-memory queues may lose messages on restart.

sampleQuestions.question: An architect needs to see which applications call which APIs across the estate. Which tool helps visualize these dependencies?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Anypoint Visualizer shows relationships and dependencies among APIs and applications.
whyWrong: Exchange catalogs assets but does not visualize application dependencies.
Visualizer shows API and application relationships.
Design Center is used for design work rather than estate visualization.

sampleQuestions.question: Every API must require a client ID before consumers can call it. How can this be enforced consistently?
options: Apply Client ID Enforcement through API Manager
Ask each team to add a separate code check
Review every API manually before release
sampleQuestions.explanation: API Manager can apply a Client ID Enforcement policy consistently to managed APIs.
whyWrong: API Manager can enforce registered client credentials at runtime.
Code checks vary by team and are harder to govern consistently.
Manual review does not enforce authentication on each call.

sampleQuestions.question: New API specifications must meet naming and security standards before publication. What should the organization use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: API Governance rulesets can check specifications against organizational standards.
whyWrong: VPC peering connects networks, not specification standards.
Load balancers manage traffic rather than API design rules.
Governance rulesets can check API specifications against standards.

sampleQuestions.question: Which pair of targets should drive a disaster recovery design?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Recovery time and recovery point objectives express acceptable downtime and data loss.
whyWrong: Recovery objectives describe acceptable downtime and data loss.
Team size and API count do not define recovery targets.
Business group count does not specify failover expectations.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an Anypoint VPC provide?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Anypoint VPC provides network isolation and private connectivity for CloudHub applications.
whyWrong: An Anypoint VPC provides private network isolation and connectivity for CloudHub applications.
Exchange stores and shares assets rather than providing a network.
Monitoring dashboards display operations data but do not provide private networking.

sampleQuestions.question: A stateless CloudHub application is under heavier traffic and response time is rising. What is a straightforward first step?
options: Switch to a shared load balancer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Adding replicas can scale a stateless application horizontally to handle more traffic.
whyWrong: Replicas can add capacity for a stateless application.
A shared load balancer does not add application compute capacity alone.
Changing to customer-hosted runtime is a larger change than scaling replicas.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should an organization prevent teams from deploying directly to production without review?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Environment permissions and roles can restrict who is allowed to deploy to production.
whyWrong: Compute sizing does not grant deployment permission.
Monitoring does not control who can deploy.
Deleting the environment is not a workable approval control.

sampleQuestions.question: A platform team needs Anypoint-managed deployments and monitoring for Mule apps running on its Kubernetes clusters. Which option provides that integration?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Runtime Fabric links customer-operated Kubernetes infrastructure with Anypoint Platform deployment and monitoring capabilities.
whyWrong: Exchange catalogs assets rather than deploying to customer Kubernetes.
CloudHub runs in MuleSoft-managed infrastructure.
Studio is a development environment rather than a runtime deployment option.
